title: Sustained net-electric power from controlled fusion

concept.text: The innovation is a controlled fusion facility that supplies more electrical energy than the entire facility consumes over sustained operation. Fusion joins light atomic nuclei and releases energy; an electricity-producing plant must capture that energy, convert it to electricity and retain a surplus after powering its own equipment. Both inertial confinement, which compresses individual fuel targets, and magnetic confinement, which confines hot plasma with magnetic fields, fall within this concept.

Conceptual distinction: target gain compares fusion energy with energy delivered to a target; plasma gain compares fusion output with energy supplied to heat the plasma; facility-level electrical gain accounts for electricity generation and consumption across the whole plant. These quantities use different boundaries and cannot be substituted for one another. A successful individual fusion experiment therefore does not by itself demonstrate a power station. The proposed advance combines plasma and nuclear physics with materials, heat extraction, electrical conversion and reliable plant operation.

significance.text: If demonstrated, sustained fusion-powered net electrical export would establish controlled fusion as a new primary electricity source. That is a reasoned consequence of the proposed capability, grounded in the demonstrated release of energy through light-nucleus fusion. The fusion reaction itself does not involve carbon combustion. LLNL's burning-plasma experiments establish an important physical foundation, while CFS's projected ARC plant illustrates the intended transition from fusion experiments to electricity generation.

Conditional impact assessment: a repeatable electrical surplus would establish energy production, but would not by itself establish affordable electricity or widespread deployment. Lower-cost power and wider industrial use would depend on construction costs, operating availability, maintenance, fuel supply and component replacement. A deuterium–tritium plant would also need an adequate tritium supply; fuel self-sufficiency would be an additional achievement. Neither a brief net-electric demonstration nor a high target gain establishes decades of component life, low lifecycle emissions or commercial competitiveness.

Scientific distinction: fusion should not be described simply as having no chain reaction without explaining the intended comparison. Burning-plasma operation includes feedback in which fusion products help heat the fuel and sustain further reactions. The meaningful advance here is controlled operation with a measured electrical surplus; neither a broad analogy with fission nor a claim of inherent commercial simplicity establishes that result.

missing_breakthrough.text: The sought capability is an integrated facility that maintains a positive electrical balance during sustained fusion operation. LLNL's reported target-energy comparison does not establish that capability: energy delivered to a target is only one part of a plant's energy budget. CFS's June 2026 announcement describes continuous net electricity as a future ARC outcome. Neither retained source reports a facility-level net-electric demonstration, although these two sources cannot establish worldwide nonachievement through 1 November 2026.

Engineering synthesis: sufficient fusion yield must be combined with efficient drivers or plasma heating, energy capture and electrical conversion so that auxiliary consumption leaves a useful surplus. Inertial approaches must turn separate shots into sufficiently frequent, repeatable operation, with viable target production and injection and a chamber that survives repeated events. Magnetic approaches must sustain adequate confinement, heating and control while integrating the equipment needed for power production. The supplied review does not quantify these losses or establish how close any particular design is to closing its electrical balance.

Engineering synthesis: practical operation also requires materials and components that tolerate the relevant heat and radiation exposure, reliable heat removal, maintainable plant systems and a workable fuel cycle. For deuterium–tritium designs, tritium availability and eventual self-sufficiency are distinct challenges. Target economics, repetition rate and chamber durability remain relevant even though none is settled by the definition of target gain. These are integration requirements and barriers to practical use, not a claim that every one must be fully solved before an initial net-electric experiment.

current_state.text: LLNL reports that NIF first exceeded target gain on 5 December 2022, producing 3.15 MJ of fusion energy from 2.05 MJ of laser energy delivered to the target. On 7 April 2025, it produced 8.6 MJ ± 0.45 MJ from 2.08 MJ of laser energy, with target gain 4.13. Its 11th ignition experiment, on 20 June 2026, yielded 7.9 MJ ± 0.4 MJ, with gain approximately 3.8. These are reported experimental results, including the stated yield uncertainties.

Those NIF results concern individual shots in a facility supporting stockpile science. LLNL's target-gain comparison uses fusion yield and laser energy delivered to the target; it is not a whole-facility electrical balance or a demonstration of electrical export. The page also discusses ignition through capsule heating and burning-plasma feedback, so target gain above one should not be presented as a universal definition of ignition. The supplied evidence does not quantify NIF's total electrical consumption relative to these yields.

In its 4 June 2026 announcement, Commonwealth Fusion Systems described five Journal of Plasma Physics papers supporting the physics basis of a future ARC tokamak. The company projected approximately 400 MW of continuous net electricity and described a path to grid electricity in the early 2030s. These are future plant projections associated with modeling and design work, not measured ARC output. The announcement also described starting SPARC operations as a future step, supporting that operational description specifically at the announcement date.

The supplied review had complete, untruncated saved texts of the LLNL page and the CFS announcement, with no recorded extraction issues. Its CFS evidence was the company announcement rather than the underlying journal collection: the papers were not supplied or inspected, and the supplied overview DOI was not authenticated against a paper. Neither retained document reports demonstrated net electricity from fusion. Their substantive coverage extends to June 2026 results and plans; no bounded search or freshness record establishes comprehensive coverage of later developments through 1 November 2026. These limits constrain the status conclusion without showing that the reported experiments or projections are false.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: operate a fusion facility continuously for hours, or over a high-duty-cycle operating day, and show a positive net electrical export across a declared whole-facility boundary. Meter electrical exports and imports separately, then establish that exports exceed imports after correcting for stored-energy changes and accounting for other energy inputs. Report total electrical generation and facility consumption so that the surplus can be independently reconstructed. Hours or an operating day are proposed evidentiary thresholds, not established standards.
completion_criteria.label: Whole-facility electrical surplus over hours or high-duty-cycle operating day

completion_criteria.text: Proposed accounting protocol: include the systems required for operation, such as drivers or heating, magnets where applicable, cooling, fuel and target handling, and electrical conversion. Specify any excluded equipment and justify the boundary. Compare initial and final stored-energy inventories, including batteries, capacitors and thermal stores, or subtract their net contribution. Measure fusion products and the associated energy flow to demonstrate that fusion accounts for the surplus. A single shot with fusion yield above laser energy delivered to the target would not meet these criteria.
completion_criteria.label: Whole-facility energy accounting demonstrates a fusion-derived electrical surplus

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical reporting: use independently checked metering, publish uncertainty estimates and operating records, and repeat the result in a separate campaign under a disclosed protocol. Report run duration, duty cycle, interruptions, fuel consumption, maintenance and component degradation. Successful tests would establish net-electric operation within the tested conditions and durations; they would not establish unrestricted operating breadth, long-term reliability, economic viability or fuel self-sufficiency. Those broader claims require additional demonstrations.
completion_criteria.label: Independently checked net-electric operation reproduced under a disclosed protocol

related_concepts.text: Roster comparison — PHY-01, Ambient-pressure superconducting conductors at room temperature: improved superconducting conductors could be relevant to magnetic-confinement equipment and its operating burden. Such conductors would not themselves establish fusion confinement, energy conversion or a facility electrical surplus. Conversely, this fusion concept does not require the separate achievement of room-temperature superconductivity at ambient pressure.

Roster comparison — PHY-10, Collider-quality plasma wakefield acceleration, and PHY-09, A coherent gamma-ray source: these share broad experimental territory involving energetic particles, plasmas or radiation. Their defining outputs are a collider-quality accelerator and a coherent radiation source, respectively. Neither output demonstrates electricity generation, and a fusion power demonstration would not establish either capability.

Roster comparison — PHY-03, A laboratory proof that gravity is non-classical; PHY-04, Laboratory identification of the dark-matter particle; PHY-05, A tested microphysical account of the dark-energy scale; PHY-06, Discovery of a magnetic monopole; PHY-07, Observation of baryon-number violation; PHY-08, Observation of lepton-number violation; PHY-11, A tested resolution of the black-hole information paradox; PHY-12, Experimental identification of the physics that sets the Higgs-mass scale; and PHY-13, A tested mechanism for the cosmic matter excess are distinct discovery or explanatory goals. Fusion power instead seeks an integrated energy-producing capability. Their shared placement in physics does not imply that any of these discoveries is a prerequisite for controlled fusion electricity or would follow from its demonstration.

unresolved_issues: The supplied evidence does not establish whether any other project demonstrated facility-level net electricity, or whether relevant developments occurred after June 2026 and before 1 November 2026.
NIF's whole-facility electrical balance and the magnitude of its electrical losses are not supplied.
The underlying ARC journal papers, their assumptions and their support for the projected net output remain unexamined in the supplied review; the overview DOI remains unauthenticated against a paper.
The evidence does not quantify how close particular fusion designs are to overcoming repetition-rate, materials, fuel-cycle, conversion-efficiency or economic barriers.

A definitive demonstration protocol still needs agreed facility boundaries, uncertainty tolerances and treatment of startup, shutdown, supporting equipment and stored energy. The proposed durations are not established standards.

Long-term component life, tritium self-sufficiency where applicable, availability and commercial electricity cost would remain separate questions after an initial sustained net-electric demonstration.

brief.title: Power stations fueled by joining atoms
possible: Your electricity could come from a power station that joins light atomic cores to release energy, a process called fusion. It would supply electricity steadily while producing enough to run all its own equipment and leave a surplus for the grid.
why: This would establish fusion as a new primary source of electricity for homes and industry. The reaction releases energy without burning carbon.

sources.who: Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory and collaborators
sources.showed: Their laser experiments repeatedly achieved ignition, where fusion heats the fuel enough to sustain further reactions. They increased yield, the fusion energy released, and target gain, its ratio to laser energy delivered to the fuel target.
sources.quote: LLNL researchers continue to repeat the ignition achievement with increasing yield and target gain.
sources.cited_for: The experiments establish that fusion fuel can release more energy than the laser delivers to its target.
sources.not_established: Individual laser shots do not establish an electrical surplus after powering the entire facility.

sources.who: Commonwealth Fusion Systems and collaborating scientists
sources.showed: The team modeled ARC, a proposed plant that would hold hot fuel with magnetic fields. Its analysis projects continuous net electricity of about 400 megawatts.
sources.cited_for: The ARC analysis describes a proposed path from fusion physics to continuous electricity generation.
sources.not_established: The projected electrical surplus has not been demonstrated by an operating ARC plant.

shown: Lawrence Livermore’s laser experiments have repeatedly released more fusion energy than the laser delivered to the fuel target. That measures only part of the energy budget. It does not demonstrate electricity left over after running the whole facility.
missing: A working facility would have to capture fusion energy, convert it to electricity and sustain a surplus after powering its equipment.
Operation would have to continue through sustained fuel confinement or frequent, repeatable shots.
Heat removal, durable components and a workable fuel supply would have to function together during power production.

milestones.label: A whole plant exports surplus electricity over sustained operation
milestones.explanation: A facility would have to export more electricity than it imports over hours or a day spent mostly operating, accounting for stored energy and other inputs. This would establish a sustained electrical surplus.

milestones.label: Full energy accounting attributes the surplus to fusion
milestones.explanation: Measurements would have to account for operating equipment and stored energy, and trace the surplus to fusion. This would rule out a surplus supplied by overlooked inputs or depleted energy stores.

milestones.label: Independent checks confirm a repeated electrical surplus
milestones.explanation: A separate campaign would have to repeat the result with independently checked meters, disclosed methods, uncertainties and operating records. This would establish repeatability under the tested conditions.

uncertain: The required operating duration, facility boundary and acceptable measurement uncertainty still need agreed standards.
How close different designs are to solving fuel supply, component wear and efficient electricity conversion remains uncertain.
An initial electrical surplus would leave long-term reliability, fuel self-sufficiency and competitive electricity costs unresolved.

page.title: Net electricity from controlled fusion
page.definition: A controlled-fusion plant converts energy released by joining light atomic nuclei into electricity and supplies a surplus after powering all plant equipment. For a pulsed plant, the balance includes both the pulses and the intervals between them over a continuous run. A laboratory target can release more fusion energy than the laser light it receives while the facility still draws electricity from the grid.

goal.need: Global electricity demand grew by about 800 TWh, or 3%, in 2025, and fossil fuels still supplied more than half of generation. Fusion could give grid operators another low-carbon source of electricity when demand stays high and wind or solar output falls. Only the surplus after the plant powers itself is available to customers. Its value to them depends on whether commercial plants can deliver that power reliably and at a competitive cost.

completion.title: A fusion plant delivers DOE’s example of significant net output: more than 50 MW for more than three hours.
completion.criterion: Demonstrate the numerical example in DOE’s pilot-plant definition: >50 MWe of net fusion electricity for >3 continuous hours. Net output subtracts all facility electrical consumption, including drivers or plasma heating, magnets, cooling and other auxiliaries. For pulsed concepts, evaluate time-averaged electrical output over repeated pulses during continuous plant operation. The >50 MWe value is DOE’s example of a significant output, rather than a universal minimum.
completion.set_by: U.S. Department of Energy, Milestone-Based Fusion Development Program, DE-FOA-0002809, footnote 11. The power value is explicitly illustrative.
completion.threshold_quote: An FPP should demonstrate a significant amount of net fusion electricity (e.g., >50 MWe) for >3 continuous hours
completion.basis: DOE gives more than 50 MW as an example of significant net electrical output and specifies more than three continuous hours. The National Academies’ Phase 1b distinguishes peak electrical power from positive electrical gain averaged over the run. DOE also asks for a path to one full-power year. That later objective bears on component life and availability.

milestones.title: Fusion products supply more than half of a plasma’s heating.
milestones.criterion: Heating deposited in the plasma by fusion products must exceed external heating of the plasma. For an inertial implosion, evaluate the transient energy balance in the fuel and compare deposited fusion heating with the mechanical work of compression.
milestones.set_by: DOE Office of Science, “DOE Explains...Burning Plasma”; the inertial-case application and experimental tests are given by Zylstra and colleagues.
milestones.threshold_quote: A plasma enters what scientists call the burning plasma regime when the self-heating power exceeds any external heating.

milestones.title: Fusion output exceeds the external energy delivered to the target or plasma.
milestones.criterion: Scientific gain must exceed one. For a driven target, divide fusion yield by total driver energy delivered to the target. For a magnetically confined plasma, divide fusion power by external heating power delivered to the plasma. For a magneto-inertial pulse, identify the target or plasma boundary used and account for all energy delivered across it to heat and compress the fuel during that pulse.
milestones.set_by: Scientific-breakeven convention: DOE’s 2022 NIF announcement states the inertial-target test; ITER’s FAQs state the magnetic-plasma test.
milestones.threshold_quote: more energy from fusion than the laser energy used to drive it.

milestones.title: A fusion device produces 100–500 MW of time-averaged thermal power for at least 100 seconds.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate the Phase 1a target of 100–500 MW of time-averaged fusion thermal power for ≥100 s, exceeding characteristic plasma and power-removal timescales. Demonstrate sufficient plasma gain to make net electricity feasible in subsequent pilot phases. Pulsed concepts operate at the design repetition rate for Phase 2. This integration stage precedes electricity production in Phase 1b.
milestones.set_by: National Academies, Bringing Fusion to the U.S. Grid, Phase 1a. Its phase framework is applied in the peer-reviewed ARC physics basis.
milestones.threshold_quote: 100-500 MW time-averaged thermal power for ≥100 s

milestones.title: A laboratory confinement system produces measurable fusion reactions in heated fuel.
milestones.criterion: Detect fusion products from the confined fuel and establish that their measured properties are consistent with reactions between thermal fuel ions. Neutron detection alone is insufficient when accelerated particles could account for the signal.
milestones.set_by: International Energy Agency, experimental proof of concept at technology readiness level 3. The Scylla experiments illustrate how fusion-product measurements establish thermonuclear origin.
milestones.threshold_quote: the confinement system can produce fusion

milestones.title: A fusion reactor reaches engineering breakeven at 1–100 MW of thermal power for at least 10 minutes.
milestones.criterion: Operate at 1–100 MW of thermal power for at least 10 minutes. Over that interval, fusion energy output must at least equal all energy inputs to produce the fuel, sustain the reaction and operate the plant. This test uses fusion energy output before conversion to electricity.
milestones.set_by: International Energy Agency, The State of Energy Innovation 2026, fusion technology readiness level 5.
milestones.threshold_quote: 1 MWth to 100 MWth scale with engineering breakeven for periods of at least 10 minutes

definition = "A controlled-fusion plant converts energy released by joining light atomic nuclei into electricity and supplies a surplus after powering all plant equipment. For a pulsed plant, the balance includes both the pulses and the intervals between them over a continuous run. A laboratory target can release more fusion energy than the laser light it receives while the facility still draws electricity from the grid.". Reason: The existing definition leaves unclear whether a pulsed plant must supply a surplus at every instant and how plant output differs from target gain.

goal.need = "Global electricity demand grew by about 800 TWh, or 3%, in 2025, and fossil fuels still supplied more than half of generation. Fusion could give grid operators another low-carbon source of electricity when demand stays high and wind or solar output falls. Only the surplus after the plant powers itself is available to customers. Its value to them depends on whether commercial plants can deliver that power reliably and at a competitive cost.". Reason: The existing paragraph gives the scale of demand but describes a committee’s objective in place of the benefit to electricity users and the conditions for obtaining it.

add statement by UK Atomic Energy Authority, 2022: "demonstrate the ability to put net electricity on the grid". Reason: The UK’s STEP programme explicitly names net delivery to the grid as a prototype objective.

edit completion: title = "A fusion plant delivers DOE\u2019s example of significant net output: more than 50 MW for more than three hours."; basis = "DOE gives more than 50 MW as an example of significant net electrical output and specifies more than three continuous hours. The National Academies\u2019 Phase 1b distinguishes peak electrical power from positive electrical gain averaged over the run. DOE also asks for a path to one full-power year. That later objective bears on component life and availability.". Reason: The headline presents 50 MW as a fixed minimum, and the basis omits the distinction between DOE’s example and the Academies’ peak-power target.

rename case "Inertial confinement: fuel targets are compressed in individual pulses." to "Inertial confinement". Reason: The current case name includes an explanatory sentence where a confinement approach is needed as a label.

rename case "Magnetic confinement: magnetic fields confine the reacting plasma." to "Magnetic confinement". Reason: The shorter case name identifies the magnetic approach consistently across the milestone results.
add case "Magneto-inertial confinement". Reason: The NRC identifies magneto-inertial confinement as a third approach with distinct experimental results.

add milestone after None: "A laboratory confinement system produces measurable fusion reactions in heated fuel.". Reason: The current milestones begin with self-heating and omit the first experimental demonstration of fusion in confined fuel.

edit m1: criterion = "Heating deposited in the plasma by fusion products must exceed external heating of the plasma. For an inertial implosion, evaluate the transient energy balance in the fuel and compare deposited fusion heating with the mechanical work of compression.". Reason: The criterion currently names four experimental shots and gives their verdicts, which belong with the results.

edit m2: title = "Fusion output exceeds the external energy delivered to the target or plasma."; criterion = "Scientific gain must exceed one. For a driven target, divide fusion yield by total driver energy delivered to the target. For a magnetically confined plasma, divide fusion power by external heating power delivered to the plasma. For a magneto-inertial pulse, identify the target or plasma boundary used and account for all energy delivered across it to heat and compress the fuel during that pulse."; refs = [8, 5, 9, 20]. Reason: The existing criterion mixes two experimental verdicts with the test and leaves the energy-input boundary implicit for hybrid devices.

add milestone after m2: "A fusion reactor reaches engineering breakeven at 1–100 MW of thermal power for at least 10 minutes.". Reason: The IEA identifies a sustained whole-system energy balance at thermal power as an intermediate test distinct from both plasma gain and net electrical output.
remove not found 0. Reason: The phrase “either confinement approach” limits the existing search finding to two cases.

add not found: "No published experiment was found that meets milestone m3 or the electrical completion test in any of the three confinement approaches.". Reason: The published-result gap for the Phase 1a thermal target and the electrical completion test also applies to magneto-inertial confinement.
